editorial:
Imagine moving to a huge, scary city where you don't know anyone, just to make a better life for the person you love. That is exactly what Jun does when he heads to Hong Kong. He is a bit shy and naive, but he quickly meets Qiao, a smart and tough girl who knows how to survive on the streets. Their bond starts as a simple friendship between two outsiders, but it slowly grows into a deep, heartbreaking romance. The vibe is very nostalgic and sweet, making you feel the struggle of two people trying to find their way in a world that keeps pushing them apart.

What really makes this story work is the acting; you can feel their longing every time they are apart. The pacing is steady, though it might feel slow if you want a lot of action, but the emotional payoff is huge. If you love stories about fate and missed connections, you have to see this. Since it is an older film, you should try to find a high-quality restoration. If you can, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night in.
endingExplained: After years of being apart and living in different cities, Jun and Qiao finally cross paths again in New York City. They happen to be at the same place at the same time by total chance. They realize that despite all the years, the distance, and the other people in their lives, they still love each other. They embrace in the street, finally ending their long cycle of missing each other and deciding to be together for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about destiny and long-distance love.
